entities.summary: Sevda Sevan was a prominent Armenian-Bulgarian writer and diplomat who played a crucial role in promoting cultural exchange between Armenia and Bulgaria during the late 20th century. Born in 1945 in Nova Zagora, Bulgaria, Sevda Sevan was a key figure in the Bulgarian literary scene, known for his works on Bulgarian-Armenian relations and the history of the Armenian diaspora. As the Ambassador of Armenia in Bulgaria from 1994 to 2005, Sevda Sevan worked tirelessly to strengthen ties between the two countries and promote mutual understanding. Sevda Sevan was also the third wife of Bulgarian writer and editor Varban Stamatov, with whom he collaborated on several literary projects. Through his diplomatic efforts and literary works, Sevda Sevan left a lasting legacy in the realms of Armenian-Bulgarian relations and Bulgarian literature. Despite his passing in 2009, Sevda Sevan's work continues to inspire new generations of scholars and writers.
